summary: This is a test suite that automated checks that a website works correctly by visiting different pages and verifying they contain expected content. It tests things like whether the homepage loads, whether blog posts appear, whether navigation works, and whether error pages display properly.

explanations.3: The `it()` function defines a single test case with a description and a callback function that contains the actual test logic.
explanations.4: getenv('WEBSITE') retrieves an environment variable containing the website's URL, so the tests can run against any configured site without hardcoding the address.
explanations.5: The arrow notation `->` chains method calls together; assertSee() checks that the text 'Avonture' appears somewhere on the page that was visited.
explanations.14: Concatenating a string onto the URL with `.` adds '/blog' to the base website URL to test a specific page.
explanations.20: The click() method simulates a user clicking on an element with the text 'Blog' on the page.
explanations.21: assertPathIs() verifies that after the click, the browser ended up at the expected URL path '/blog'.
explanations.37: click() with a CSS selector like '.DocSearch-Button' finds and clicks the element matching that selector instead of searching by text.
explanations.38: type() simulates a user typing text into a form input field identified by the CSS selector '.DocSearch-Input'.
